correctness.rationale: The quotient-distance formula follows from convexity of upper-half-plane horoballs. The memoryless property yields independent Exp(1) height separation and Exp(2) minimum, giving a triangular rescaled horizontal displacement. A quadratic root test is exact once R >= 2 arsinh(w/4). Uniform fixed-width expansion gives the e^-R, w^2 e^-3R/24, and (w^2/24+w^4/120)e^-5R terms with O_w(e^-7R) remainder. A common-variable coupling proves strict stochastic order for every positive threshold and the tail controls all exponential moments. Independently computed standard-library quadrature and 1,100,000 simulated upper-half-plane pairs passed; experiments support rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The two-point distance distribution is an intrinsic geometric invariant on a canonical noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. Its universal leading tail conceals the boundary horocycle length while the first curvature/quotient correction determines that length exactly; this gives an inverse-rigidity result. The strict stochastic order and sharp exponential integrability threshold add motivated structural conclusions with geometric and probabilistic utility.
